title: Spec context
description: One repository's spec context file (<work>/spec-<slug>.context.json), handed to its spec authors, its spec reviewer and its task decomposer as `repository context`. The step `spec_authoring.context` (orchestrator/flows/spec_authoring.py) writes it and validates it against this file. It holds facts and pointers only: what binds the Story's stacks (constraints, shared capabilities, TRD requirements) is in the spec pack beside it (spec-pack.schema.json), and the text of the headings `documents` names is read with `atw-matrix heading`, never copied here. Every design detail a spec needs was decided during architecture and is in those documents and the matrix; a spec states the build work and decides none of it.

slug.description: The repository's slug, as the work files name it.

frontend.description: Whether the repository is a frontend repository, whose UI items get design sources.

items.description: Where this repository's Story builds: the span's items placed in this repository (target-report.schema.json, DeltaItem, with the repository's slug), each an element the Epic's architecture adds or changes or, for an Epic whose architecture changes nothing, an element that realizes a feature the Epic's requirements are served by. What the spec covers for each is in `buildScope`. An event item carries the event's description, its trigger and its producers (`publishedBy`).

stacks.description: Each stack the Story builds in, with the matrix ids of the entries the Story builds in it. `atw-matrix story-scope --stack <stack> --ids <entries>` prints the documents and headings that describe the stack and each entry, the constraints that bind them and the shared capabilities they must use; `atw-matrix uses --ids <entries>` prints the shared capabilities alone, each with what it provides and what its consumers must do.

documents.description: The architecture documents (arc42 and the detailed architecture) the story scopes of `stacks` name, each with its id, its file and the headings to read (none when a scope names the document as a whole). `atw-matrix heading '<path>#<heading>'` prints a heading's text as the vault's last commit holds it (a path alone, the document's whole body); cite a document by the path and heading given here.

buildScope.description: What the spec covers for each entry the Story builds, decided from the entry's verified state in the matrix, never from an architecture delta. `delta`: the entry is verified, so nothing it must be built as has changed since its last build and test, and the spec covers this Epic's own work for it alone (such as the wording of a page). `full`: the entry is not verified (a change cleared the flag, or it was never built), so the spec covers all the work that brings the build up to the entry's approved architecture.

verified.description: Whether the entry carries the verified mark.

componentDocuments.description: Every architecture and design document (arc42 and the detailed architecture under `detailed/`) of the component the Story builds: each document `atw-matrix documents --id` joins to a stack the Story builds in or an entry it builds, with its file. The step that writes the Story document ends every spec document with links to these, so whoever builds from the spec has the full architecture of the component.

dependsOn.description: Each dependency relationship from something the Story builds to something it does not build: context, never work.

prd.description: The PRD's path. The TRD states every obligation with its PRD heading as its source; open the PRD only to read a heading a TRD requirement cites, when the requirement's text does not settle a detail.

architectureResult.description: The solutions architect's result (architecture-result.schema.json). Its `facts` name the home document and heading of each design fact this Epic's architecture decided, in arc42 or in the detailed architecture under `detailed/`: for an entry whose scope is `delta`, these facts are the change the spec covers.

designSystem.description: The dispatch's design system facts (the driver surface's `designSystem` argument); empty when the dispatch gives none.

StackEntries.description: One stack and the matrix ids of the entries a Story builds in it.

DependsOn.description: One dependency of something a Story builds on something it does not build. `side` is the side that states the relationship: one with `side: repository` is a hint read from code, never an architecture fact. `stack` and `repository` are the far end's; `builtBy` is the storyKey of another Story of this Epic whose items include `to`, or null.
